title: GA4GH IO Profile File Keywords
description: Keywords that describe file parameters: file references and the structure of tabular files.

x-ga4gh-tabular-schema.description: Experimental. A nested JSON schema describing the rows of a tabular file (e.g., a sample sheet), as a hint for clients (e.g., to offer a spreadsheet editor). Not a validation rule: validation of tabular files is deferred. Checked by the same rules as every other schema of the IO schema ($defs/subschemas of the meta-schema).

allOf.$comment: dependentSchemas is wrapped in an allOf: Ajv drops the properties that this schema evaluates (properties) when dependentSchemas sits next to them and its keyword is absent, and would reject them as unevaluated.

x-ga4gh-file.$comment: A file reference is a flat string schema. The profile defines its value syntax, not `format` (e.g., `uri` rejects compact DRS identifiers); `contentMediaType`, `contentEncoding` and `contentSchema` describe the string itself, not the referenced file. In-place applicators are not allowed on the annotated schema, so that it stays flat for converters and clients. This checks only the annotated schema: schemas that apply at the same location (e.g., a sibling in a parent allOf) can't be checked here; the specification forbids them to add these keywords.

fileReference.description: Marks a string as a reference to a file or directory and describes what it refers to.

kind.description: Whether the string refers to a file or to a directory.

mediaType.description: Media type of the referenced file (RFC 6838, e.g., text/csv), without parameters.

ontology.description: HTTP(S) IRI of an ontology term for the format of the referenced file or directory (e.g., an EDAM format term), with namespace prefixes expanded.

compression.description: Compression of the referenced file. bgzip is block-compressed gzip: gzip tools read it, and index tools (e.g., tabix) need it.

secondaryFiles.description: Files that must exist next to the referenced file (e.g., indexes), as suffix patterns in the style of CWL with at least one character other than a dot: the suffix is appended to the name of the referenced file, after each leading ^ has removed one extension (e.g., .bai for sample.bam.bai, ^.bai for sample.bai).

schemes.description: URI schemes that values may use (e.g., drs, https, s3), in lowercase. If given, values must be absolute URIs with one of them; paths are not allowed. The schemes javascript, vbscript, livescript, data, blob, filesystem, file, jar, view-source and about are rejected; for all others, the deployment's allow-list is the control.

then.$comment: Media types, compression and secondary files apply to files only.
